confidence_notes: The food and drink figures come from two web searches. A cost-of-living search returned aggregated, crowd-sourced Lucerne price ranges from traveltables.com and thecurrencyshop.com.au: about CHF 20-30 for a cheap meal, CHF 4-6 or about CHF 5 for a cappuccino, and CHF 6-8 for a 0.5 L draught beer. These figures were collected between 2023 and mid-2025 and are only as quoted in search summaries. The pages were not opened. The figures were adjusted up a little for July 2026 peak-season tourist pricing. CHF was converted to USD at about 1.25 USD per CHF. That rate is a model assumption and was not looked up. The mid-range meal is based on a Numbeo-derived figure of about USD 124 from 2023, adjusted for inflation and Lucerne's above-average restaurant prices. The cocktail and wine estimates have no direct search data. They are based on the usual Swiss price ratio to beer, roughly 2.5x beer for a cocktail and 1.3x beer for a glass of wine, so they are less certain. The accommodation figures are holistic estimates from general knowledge of July peak-season prices in Lucerne. No booking sites or live listings were checked, so these are the least certain anchors. The RBA rate of 0.6720 for 18 November 2026 comes from a search result that quotes the RBA Exchange Rates Overview page. The RBA page itself was not opened, and one secondary source quoted a different earlier print.
comparable_city_reasoning: Lucerne is treated as a high-cost Swiss tourist city. Restaurant prices are comparable to or slightly above the Swiss average, close to Zurich and Interlaken, and peak summer demand pushes up hotel and hostel rates.
